analyst.summary: A command-line to-do list for one user. Tasks have a title, an optional due date and a done flag, and are kept in a local file between runs.

requirements.title: Add a task
requirements.description: The user can add a task with a title and an optional due date.
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty list, when the user adds 'Buy milk', then the list contains one open task 'Buy milk'.
Given a due date in the format YYYY-MM-DD, when the task is added, then the task shows that due date.

requirements.title: List tasks
requirements.description: The user can list all tasks with their number, title, due date and status.
acceptance_criteria: Given two tasks, when the user lists tasks, then both appear with numbers 1 and 2 in the order they were added.

requirements.title: Complete a task
requirements.description: The user can mark a task as done by its number.
acceptance_criteria: Given an open task 1, when the user completes task 1, then task 1 is shown as done.
Given no task 5, when the user completes task 5, then an error message names the missing number.

requirements.title: Delete a task
requirements.description: The user can delete a task by its number.
acceptance_criteria: Given tasks 1 and 2, when the user deletes task 1, then only the former task 2 remains.

requirements.title: Persist tasks
requirements.description: Tasks are saved to a JSON file after every change and loaded at start.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task was added, when the program is restarted, then the task is still listed.

assumptions: The JSON file lives next to the program unless a path is configured.

analyst:chat: REQ-005 (Persist tasks) comes from your answer to Q3 ('Yes, store them in a file'). Storing JSON after every change is my assumption; it is listed under assumptions, so you can revise it if you prefer saving only on exit.

architect.notes: A small layered design: a CLI front end, a TaskService with the use cases and a JsonTaskRepository for persistence. Open point: whether due dates should be validated as real calendar dates.

diagrams.name: Use cases
diagrams.rationale: One actor, four goals. Persistence is not a use case because the user never asks for it; it is a quality of every use case.

diagrams.name: Domain classes
diagrams.rationale: Task is a plain value object. TaskService holds the use cases so the CLI stays thin; the repository hides the JSON file so tests can use an in-memory one. Rejected: putting persistence into Task.

diagrams.name: Complete a task
diagrams.rationale: The most error-prone scenario: the number may not exist, so the alternative path is shown. Saving happens after every change (REQ-005).
diagrams.plantuml:
@startuml
actor User
participant Cli
participant TaskService
participant JsonTaskRepository
User -> Cli : todo done 1
Cli -> TaskService : complete(1)
TaskService -> JsonTaskRepository : load()
JsonTaskRepository --> TaskService : tasks
alt task 1 exists
  TaskService -> JsonTaskRepository : save(tasks)
  TaskService --> Cli : task
  Cli --> User : "1 Buy milk [done]"
else no such task
  TaskService --> Cli : error
  Cli --> User : "No task number 1"
end
@enduml

architect:chat: TaskService sits between the Cli and the repository (Domain classes diagram) so that the use cases REQ-001 to REQ-004 can be tested without a terminal and without a file. The alternative, letting the Cli talk to the JSON file directly, would mix input parsing, rules and storage in one place.

reviewer.summary: A small, consistent layered design. Two gaps: who assigns task numbers is not modelled, and no view shows where the data lives.

findings.finding: Task.number must stay unique across runs, but no class in the diagram is responsible for handing out numbers.
findings.suggestion: Add next_number(): int to TaskRepository and let TaskService use it.

findings.finding: No diagram shows the runtime parts: one CLI process and a JSON file on disk.
findings.suggestion: Add a component diagram with the CLI, the service, the repository and tasks.json.

findings.finding: Deleting a task (REQ-004) has no interaction diagram, although it changes numbering as well.
findings.suggestion: Add a sequence for deleting a task, or state in the notes why it is not needed.

"""Entry point: python -m todo <command>. The data file is tasks.json, or TODO_FILE if set."""

import os
import sys

from todo.cli import Cli
from todo.repository import JsonTaskRepository
from todo.service import TaskService


def main() -> int:
    repository = JsonTaskRepository(os.environ.get("TODO_FILE", "tasks.json"))
    return Cli(TaskService(repository)).run(sys.argv[1:])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

tester.notes: Seven tests, one or more per acceptance criterion; an in-memory repository keeps them fast, tmp_path checks the JSON file. Not tested: the exact wording of the list output.

files.purpose: Acceptance criteria of REQ-001 to REQ-005.
files.content:
"""Tests derived from the acceptance criteria. Each test name carries the requirement it checks."""

from datetime import date

from todo.cli import Cli
from todo.models import Task
from todo.repository import JsonTaskRepository, TaskRepository
from todo.service import TaskService


class MemoryRepository(TaskRepository):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.tasks: list[Task] = []

    def load(self) -> list[Task]:
        return [Task(t.number, t.title, t.due, t.done) for t in self.tasks]

    def save(self, tasks: list[Task]) -> None:
        self.tasks = [Task(t.number, t.title, t.due, t.done) for t in tasks]


def make() -> TaskService:
    return TaskService(MemoryRepository())


def test_req_001_add_task_to_empty_list():
    service = make()
    service.add("Buy milk")
    assert [(t.title, t.done) for t in service.list()] == [("Buy milk", False)]


def test_req_001_add_task_with_due_date():
    task = make().add("Pay rent", date(2026, 12, 1))
    assert task.due == date(2026, 12, 1)


def test_req_002_list_in_the_order_added():
    service = make()
    service.add("First")
    service.add("Second")
    assert [(t.number, t.title) for t in service.list()] == [(1, "First"), (2, "Second")]


def test_req_003_complete_a_task():
    service = make()
    service.add("Buy milk")
    service.complete(1)
    assert service.list()[0].done


def test_req_003_missing_number_names_it():
    lines: list[str] = []
    code = Cli(make(), out=lines.append).run(["done", "5"])
    assert code == 1 and "5" in lines[-1]


def test_req_004_delete_a_task():
    service = make()
    service.add("First")
    service.add("Second")
    service.delete(1)
    assert [t.title for t in service.list()] == ["Second"]


def test_req_005_tasks_survive_a_restart(tmp_path):
    path = str(tmp_path / "tasks.json")
    TaskService(JsonTaskRepository(path)).add("Buy milk")
    assert [t.title for t in TaskService(JsonTaskRepository(path)).list()] == ["Buy milk"]

deployer.notes: A small Docker image with the data in a volume, and start scripts for both worlds. The component diagram has one process and one file, so one container and one volume.

files.purpose: Container image: the todo package, data in /data.
files.content:
# The to-do CLI in a small image. Tasks are kept in the /data volume.
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY todo/ ./todo/
ENV TODO_FILE=/data/tasks.json
VOLUME ["/data"]
ENTRYPOINT ["python", "-m", "todo"]
CMD ["list"]

files.purpose: Start script for macOS and Linux.
files.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Run the to-do CLI (macOS, Linux). Tasks are kept in tasks.json next to this script.
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
TODO_FILE="${TODO_FILE:-tasks.json}" exec python3 -m todo "$@"

# Run the to-do CLI on Windows. Tasks are kept in tasks.json next to this script.
Set-Location $PSScriptRoot
if (-not $env:TODO_FILE) { $env:TODO_FILE = "tasks.json" }
python -m todo @args

files.purpose: How to build and run, and where the data lives.
files.content:
# Deploy and run

Without Docker (Python 3.12):

    ./run.sh add "Buy milk" --due 2026-12-01      # macOS, Linux
    .\\run.ps1 list                                  # Windows PowerShell

With Docker:

    docker build -t todo .
    docker run --rm -v todo-data:/data todo add "Buy milk"
    docker run --rm -v todo-data:/data todo list

The tasks live in tasks.json (scripts) or in the todo-data volume (Docker).

deployer:chat: The container keeps tasks in a named volume, so they survive when the container is removed; the scripts keep them next to the program.
